summary: Regional latency spike causing timeouts — traffic routed cross-region for dedicated customer ConveyAI
description: Issue summary: ConveyAI reported intermittent 5-10s tail latency and occasional request timeouts for inference calls originating from us-east. Impact: customer requests experienced elevated p95/p99 latency and several calls timed out, causing customer-side retries and degraded product experience. Environment: Dedicated tenant on prod-us-east with fallback routing enabled to eu-west. Steps to reproduce: 1) Send batch workload (50 concurrent req/s) to customer-specific endpoint in us-east. 2) Observe increased latency at p95/p99 and occasional 504 timeouts. 3) Check routing logs for region selection. Logs/metrics: API gateway traces show spikes in request counts routed to eu-west during incident window; serving-runtime telemetry shows normal processing times in eu-west but added network RTT. Initial hypothesis: Smart-routing policy erroneously selected eu-west endpoints under capacity signal due to stale regional capacity metrics, leading to cross-region routing and increased network latency.

investigation_notes: Timeline: 09:00 UTC - customer reports. 09:10-09:20 - routing logs show 40% of ConveyAI requests routed to eu-west. 09:45 - mitigation applied (disable fallback). 10:00 - latency returns to baseline. Findings: Prometheus scrape for us-east capacity exporter rotated during scheduled infra maintenance; last successful scrape timestamp was >5m old and marked as stale. Capacity aggregator treated missing metric as zero available capacity. Smart-routing policy had no freshness threshold and immediately considered zero-capacity signal, enabling cross-region fallback. Network RTT between us-east and eu-west added ~120-180ms per request increasing tail latency and exposing timeouts for some customer request timeouts with tight client deadlines. Metrics reviewed: routing decision logs, capacity_agg metrics, api_gateway traces, tcp RTTs.
root_cause: Stale capacity telemetry caused by a Prometheus scrape rotation during maintenance; capacity aggregator interpreted stale/missing metrics as zero available capacity and triggered cross-region fallback. Smart-routing lacked a freshness threshold for capacity signals.
resolution: 1) Immediate mitigation: disabled automatic cross-region fallback for affected tenant (ConveyAI) which returned traffic to us-east and brought latency back to baseline. 2) Long-term fix: updated capacity aggregator to ignore stale scrapes (added freshness threshold of 30s) and introduced a 60s cool-down before routing will fall back across regions. 3) Added alert on spike in cross-region fallback rate and dashboard panels for tenant-level routing decisions. 4) Deployed change to production on 2026-03-01 via PR merged (see related_github_prs).
